title: Job margin analysis — two-phase contract
purpose: Report gross margin on job 7702, a single contract covering both the Phase 1 shell and the Phase 2 finishes, so the division can compare it to the interiors margin benchmark.
assertion: The margin compares the full contract value to the full cost of the same contract, on the same scope and the same cutoff.

sections.title: Job 7702 — margin to date
sections.footnote: Both phases are inside one contract. Phase 1 is closed out; Phase 2 is in progress through the cutoff.

values.memo: Phase 1 shell AND Phase 2 finishes — full contract
Interiors jobs run 12% to 15% gross margin.

variants.causeSummary: The 2,450,000 contract value covers both phases and the 2,120,000 of cost covers both phases, so revenue and cost are on the same scope through the same 9/30 cutoff. The resulting 330,000 margin, or 13.47%, sits inside the 12% to 15% benchmark and is signable.
variants.tell: Check that the cost line includes both phases before comparing it to a two-phase contract value. It does.

variants.causeSummary: Gross margin subtracts only the 1,180,000 of Phase 1 cost from the full two-phase contract value of 2,450,000, so 940,000 of Phase 2 cost is simply left out and revenue and cost no longer cover the same scope. That lifts the reported margin to 1,270,000, or 51.84%, on an interiors job whose division benchmark is 12% to 15%, and the true margin is 330,000, or 13.47%. A margin more than three times the benchmark is the signal to check scope alignment, therefore this cannot be reported to the division.
variants.tell: 51.84% on an interiors job against a 12% to 15% benchmark. The cost line used one phase while the revenue line used both.
